name: Teresa Leger Fernández
page_title: Teresa Leger Fernández's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (NM) - District 3

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "51 years ago today, Roe v. Wade established our constitutional right to reproductive freedom. A year and a half ago, SCOTUS’s decision to overturn it not only stripped away a woman's right to choose, but stole our right to privacy in our homes, marriages, and doctor’s offices."
Rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Action Fund
Voted in favor of HR 8296: "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 8297: "Ensuring Access to Abortion Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: Rated 100% by National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare

"#SocialSecurity is an earned benefit. You paid into it, and you deserve to retire with dignity. I’m glad benefits will increase by 8.7%, but we can do more to make Social Security last through 2100 and beyond. It’s a sacred trust, and I came to Congress to protect it."
"Roses are red. Violets are blue. Improving Social Security is long overdue."
Rated 100% by Alliance for Retired Americans

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "#DYK? The wealthiest pay nothing into Social Security on wages over $147,000. It’s time to lift the cap and make sure everyone pays their fair share to keep this earned benefit strong through 2100. Social Security is a sacred trust. I’m in Congress to strengthen it."
"The wealthy don’t need another tax cut – the middle class does. It’s about time that working people get the tax cut they deserve. We need to reward work in this country – not just wealth."
Rated 11% by National Taxpayers Union

positions.question: Do you support a wealth tax in order to pay for public programs?

evidence.text: "#DYK? The wealthiest pay nothing into Social Security on wages over $147,000. It’s time to lift the cap and make sure everyone pays their fair share to keep this earned benefit strong through 2100. Social Security is a sacred trust. I’m in Congress to strengthen it."

"I voted for the #BuildBackBetter Act because it delivers para la gente! It lowers the everyday costs that burden working families – from health care to child care & more. And it’s fully paid for by making big corporations & the wealthiest pay their fair share."
"It is unacceptable that millionaires will stop contributing to Social Security. I cosponsored @RepJohnLarson’s #Secure2100 to ensure everyone pays their fair share! #ScrapTheCap"
Rated 11% by National Taxpayers Union

positions.question: Do you support the regulation of indirect campaign contributions from corporations, unions, and individuals?

evidence.text: "Citizens United corrupted our politics. Special interest groups blocked actions to tackle climate change & lower prescription drug prices. Enough is enough. #HR1 will reform our campaign finance system. It’s time to put people back in charge of Washington! #DemocracyForAll"
Rated 100% by Common Cause
Voted in favor of HR 1: "For the People Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "One year after the death of #GeorgeFloyd, we continue to push for true justice. We must address system racism. We must create change. We can start by passing the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act today!"
"The Senate must pass the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act."
Voted in favor of HR 1280 "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021."

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: "The Republican appropriations bill would eliminate funding for diversity efforts in our military. That's why I spoke against it in rules last night."
Voted in favor of HR 2670: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024"
Voted in favor of HR 4350: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7900: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023"

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "As we celebrate the beauty of our planet this #EarthDay let’s use it as a reminder of our dedication to combating the #ClimateCrisis. We must continue to create clean energy jobs, build resilient infrastructure, & invest in equitable solutions to address environmental injustice."

"Now is the time to invest boldly in American families and America’s future. That’s why I am proud to support @HouseDemocrats funding bill, which will create jobs, grow opportunity for the middle class, and provide a lifeline for the nation’s most vulnerable."
Voted in favor of HR 1319 "American Rescue Plan Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Housing is essential to improve the health and wellness of children and adults. We must continue to fight for the opportunity to invest in housing resources – like rental assistance, public housing, and the Housing Trust Fund. It’s time to #BuildBackBetter"

"I secured $11.8 MILLION for small #CommunityProjects I championed across every corner of my district. These 15 projects will repair roads in Portales, help build a convention center in Questa, improve affordable housing in Santa Fe and much more!"

"New Mexico has 20,000 people struggling with homelessness – almost half of those are children with unstable housing. Today, I was proud to announce $16.5M for 28 programs across New Mexico — a step toward eliminating homelessness."

"Renters who pay more than half of their incomes on rent are 23% more likely to face food insecurity. We need to provide large-scale, sustained investments for affordable housing to ensure people have an affordable place to call home. Let's #ShowHousingLove"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "ICYMI: Yesterday, the Senate passed the #InflationReductionAct to reduce inflation and lower costs for our familias"

"Right now, Congress can alleviate some of the strain caused by inflation by passing the #BuildBackBetter Act. We can lower everyday costs for families, including childcare, health care, utility bills, prescription drugs, and education."
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022" Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7688: "Consumer Fuel Price Gouging Prevention Act"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Instead of addressing the student debt crisis, my colleagues across the aisle want to gut the SAVE Student Loan Repayment Program and make college more expensive for 5.5 million Americans — including 7,500 people in my district."
"Thanks to @POTUS, $267M in total student loan debt for New Mexico students has been forgiven. This means 6,270 New Mexicans are free of student debt. Promises made, promises kept!"

"This student loan relief is a good first step to easing the financial burden of hard working New Mexicans carrying high student loan debt. Education shouldn’t be a burden; no one should struggle with crushing debt to get a quality education."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "Today marks 57 years since the 1965 #VotingRightsAct became law. Voters are once again threatened by disenfranchisement and draconian laws. That’s why I cosponsored the #ForThePeopleAct and the John Lewis Voting Rights Act. The sacred right to vote belongs to all Americans."
Rated 100% by Common Cause
Voted in favor of HR 4: "John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5746 "Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act"

positions.question: Do you support government funding for the development of renewable energy (e.g. solar, wind, geo-thermal)?

evidence.text: "As we celebrate the beauty of our planet this #EarthDay let’s use it as a reminder of our dedication to combating the #ClimateCrisis. We must continue to create clean energy jobs, build resilient infrastructure, & invest in equitable solutions to address environmental injustice."

"I am excited to talk about renewable energy research and the creation of job opportunities for Nuevo Mexicanos. We will continue to invest in the future so that this part of New Mexico is our next Route 66 of Renewable Energy."
"I’m happy to welcome $35 million from @USDA for rural development projects! These funds will bring more renewable energy investments to Taos and help grow New Mexico’s rural economy."
Rated 97% by League of Conservation Voters

positions.question: Do you support the federal government allowing permits for drilling on public lands?

evidence.text: Voted against HR 1: "Lower Energy Costs Act"

"Fossil fuel companies have abandoned hundreds of thousands of oil and gas wells that pollute our air and water and pose serious public health risks, especially for our rural, tribal, and disadvantaged communities"
Rated 0% by American Energy Alliance
Voted against HR 21: "Strategic Production Response Act"

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "More than 31 million Americans have gained health coverage thanks to the ACA. The #BuildBackBetter Act follows through on our commitment to further expand access to care for all Americans and make health care more affordable."

"No one should have to wonder whether getting medical care is worth the cost. This pandemic has shown us that healthcare must be a human right. We need #MedicareforAll because everyone deserves access to affordable care without fear of the cost"

"The Affordable Care Act is 14 years old today! Last year, a record 21M people enrolled, many paying less than $10 per month for quality care. After building on its success with the Inflation Reduction Act, I am committed to protecting its life-changing coverage for millions."

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "More than 65 million women provided unpaid care in the form of child care, family care & eldercare during 2020. Paid leave & care policies have the potential to help the economy grow as much as 5% by bringing women’s labor force participation rates up."
"The COVID-19 pandemic has put a spotlight on working conditions for our essential workers. Workers have a right to workplace safety protections, health care, and paid leave."

"This #WomensHistoryMonth, we must continue the fight of the women who came before us. That means pushing to protect reproductive rights, invest in childcare, deliver paid leave for all, pay equity, and more"

"We can protect our rail workers and keep our supply chain moving. Today the House passed two bills to do just that. This legislation will increase worker pay by 24 percent, allow medical leave, and mandate at least 7 paid sick days annually. The Senate needs to act."

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "I came to Congress to lower prescription drug prices, protect and strengthen Social Security, and look after our elders. I’m so grateful to visit with seniors at Mary Esther Gonzales Senior Center and hear their concerns and hopes for our comunidad."

"Right now, Congress can alleviate some of the strain caused by inflation by passing the #BuildBackBetter Act. We can lower everyday costs for families, including childcare, health care, utility bills, prescription drugs, and education."

"The outrageous costs of prescription drugs forces too many Americans to ration or decline life-saving medications. The #BuildBackBetter Act caps the cost of insulin at $35 per month for every American with insurance."
Voted in favor of HR 6833 "The Affordable Insulin Now Act"
